Keep all other architecture details—including layer sizes, activation functions, optimizer, loss, batch size, and training epochs—identical to the baseline. Train both models for exactly 20 epochs and plot their validation accuracy curves on the same axes. Then, compare the two models: report the validation accuracy at epoch 20 and explain how dropout affected generalization based on the shape and gap between the curves.
payload.starter_code:
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load and preprocess data
(x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = keras.datasets.imdb.load_data(num_words=10000)
x_train = keras.preprocessing.sequence.pad_sequences(x_train, maxlen=200)
x_test = keras.preprocessing.sequence.pad_sequences(x_test, maxlen=200)

# Baseline model (overfitting)
baseline_model = keras.Sequential([
    keras.layers.Embedding(10000, 128, input_length=200),
    keras.layers.Flatten(),
    keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dense(64, activation='relu'),
    keras.layers.Dense(1, activation='sigmoid')
])

baseline_model.compile(optimizer='adam',
                       loss='binary_crossentropy',
                       metrics=['accuracy'])

# Train baseline
baseline_history = baseline_model.fit(
    x_train, y_train,
    batch_size=512,
    epochs=20,
    validation_data=(x_test, y_test),
    verbose=0
)
